lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: Light. Real light. I'd forgot the color of it. I'd forgot there was a color.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: You pulled me out. I won't forget that. I'll try to forget everything else, but not that.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: I don't rightly know. One minute I was tallying ore for the Foreman, the next the tally was in my mouth instead of the slate.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: And there was a sound under the rock. Not water. Not settling. It went like this — once for me, once for you, once for the man beside me. Like it was counting.

choices.text: Rest now. I'll handle the counting.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: You beat the Foreman. I heard his hammer going quiet from where they kept me — one blow, then none, then none.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: He was a fair man, before. Docked my wage once for a tally I hadn't earned, then paid it back double when he caught the real thief. That's the man I'd like to bury. Not the thing.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: Sister Ash keeps a candle for everyone the mine eats. Tell her I'm alive and she should light one less.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: And tell Old Tom the rungs are still counted right. I counted them every day in the dark. Going down, coming up — the numbers agreed.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: You've seen one of mine own still trapped below. Listen to me, and listen properly.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: If they answer you in my voice, ask them the tally. The Foreman docked a tally I never earned — the real one's nine measures, three slabs, and a lie. The pit doesn't know the lie.

choices.text: Nine, three, and a lie. Understood.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: They're walking up and they're smiling. That's what I can't get past. Not the walking. The smiling. It smiles the way it made me tally — with somebody else's hands.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: Whatever's wearing them wanted me next. You got me first. Don't feel bad about what you have to do to keep it that way.

choices.text: I won't let it have you.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: I keep a slate by my bed now. Every morning I tally the same nine measures, three slabs, and a lie. It keeps the counting from being done for me.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: Last night the slate was full before I touched it. Nine, three, and a lie, all neat. I'm not going to say whose hand did it. You'd stop sleeping too.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: The counting's stopped. Slate's clean this morning. First morning I haven't checked the tally in weeks.

lines.speaker: Rescued Miner
lines.text: I'm keeping the fire going, warden. Small work. Mine now.
